item.title: Wisbech man jailed for shoplifting offences
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Wisbech man jailed for shoplifting offences
A 44-year-old man from Wisbech has been sentenced to 13 months in prison for a series of shoplifting offences. Lee Thompson, of John F Kennedy Court, targeted the Tesco Express on Kirkgate Street three times between August 14 and 18. He also admitted to stealing from the Boots store in the Horsefair Shopping Centre back in May, alongside further offences committed in Norfolk.
Following his arrest by neighbourhood officers, Thompson appeared at Huntingdon Magistrates’ Court last Tuesday. The sentence includes the activation of previous suspended terms. In addition to his jail time, Thompson has been ordered to pay £99.99 in compensation. Police have thanked members of the public for reporting retail crime, noting that such information is vital for identifying offenders.

item.title: Norfolk County Council seeks feedback on recycling centres
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Norfolk County Council seeks feedback on recycling centres
Norfolk County Council is inviting residents to share their views on the county’s 19 recycling centres. An annual satisfaction survey is now open, covering sites including those in King’s Lynn, Wereham, Docking, Heacham, and Ashill.
The council says the feedback will help identify potential service improvements and understand any barriers to usage. Last year, the centres processed nearly 56,000 tonnes of household waste, with over 75 per cent diverted from general disposal. Residents can complete the short questionnaire online until October 18. Further details and the survey link are available on the Norfolk County Council website.

item.title: Inquest concludes into fatal Wisbech crash
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Inquest concludes into fatal Wisbech crash
An inquest has heard that 18-year-old Declan Berry was driving at 90mph before his car crashed into a river in Wisbech. The hearing at Cambridgeshire Coroners Court was told the vehicle, which was carrying five teenagers, hit a pothole on North Brink on March 18 before rolling into the water.
Three passengers escaped the submerged car with help from a local resident, but Mr Berry and another passenger died in the incident. Coroner Elizabeth Grey concluded that excessive speed was the primary cause of the collision, while noting that the poor condition of the road was a contributing factor. The court heard that the local council had previously received over 100 complaints regarding the state of the road.

item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
News update: QEH rebuild delay, Swaffham car park transfer and local business news
The Queen Elizabeth Hospital in King’s Lynn faces a further delay to its rebuild project, with the completion date now pushed back to 2033. Hospital leadership has confirmed that while 24-hour emergency care will continue, the potential closure of the current A&E department has not been ruled out.
In other local news, Swaffham Town Council has taken ownership of the Theatre Street and Lynn Street car parks from Breckland Council. Meanwhile, in Middleton, the former Middletons Steak House has reopened as The Middleton Crown following a major refurbishment. Finally, a new mobile mechanics service has been launched to support residents across West Norfolk, including those in the Downham, Swaffham, and Wisbech areas.
